title: Maximum Score From Grid Operations
summary: Given an n x n grid initially all white, operations involve coloring a column black from the top row down to a specified row.
statement: Given an n x n grid initially all white, operations involve coloring a column black from the top row down to a specified row. The grid score is the sum of white cells with a horizontally adjacent black cell. Determine the maximum possible score after any number of operations.
constraints: grid is a nonempty square matrix of nonnegative cell values.
Choose a black prefix height independently for every column; a cell below its column’s black prefix remains white.
Score each white cell once when at least one horizontal neighbor is black, and maximize the score.
hints: A column’s contribution depends only on its own prefix height and the maximum of its two neighbors’ heights.
DP over the previous two heights; prefix and suffix maxima evaluate all older left heights for each new right height in constant time.
Add the completed center-column prefix-sum range, shift the two-height state, then close the final column against outside height zero.
Triple-local contributions are finalized exactly when the right height becomes known; optimized maxima partition left heights by which neighbor determines exposure.
editorial: Triple-local contributions are finalized exactly when the right height becomes known; optimized maxima partition left heights by which neighbor determines exposure.

tests.explanation: Choosing compatible column heights exposes white cells totaling eleven beside black neighbors.
Exhausting the three height choices per column shows the best score is six.
